title: How Does Council Signal Enforce Monitored Containment? — Council of AI Answer-First Guide
context: 2026-09-25 EAT cycle — Council Signal is the measurement and containment layer of the Council of AI. It does not claim that any model is uncrackable. It claims that every cross-boundary interaction is observed, measured against a canonical bank, signed, and appended to an index that regulators can read.
body: Council Signal enforces monitored containment through three linked mechanisms, all operating under the principle that containment must be continuously observed and measured — never assumed from a static design review. First, the measurement board: 14 axes (detector interop, care, privacy, adversarial robustness, and others), each with a bank of 33 to 200 canonical items and a spread of 19+ model scores, frozen by an Ed25519-signed manifest. The board distinguishes true negatives from measurement noise (parse failure, format error, temperature variance) — a distinction that naive benchmarking collapses. Second, the verified measurement credential: each observation is tied to the party that measured it, the process used, and the point in time, making the claim auditable rather than promotional. The credential answers who measured, how, and whether the result is reproducible. Third, the containment index: an append-only, signed log of incidents — jailbreak chains, refusal degradation, self-exfiltration attempts, governance override attempts — that accumulates over time rather than resetting with each release. Together, these mechanisms make monitored containment operational. A deployer can point to the signed index and say: 'Here is the continuous audit evidence that the containment boundary has been tested under these conditions, with these results, by this party.' This is the opposite of a 'provable isolation' claim, which promises a boundary that engineering reality cannot deliver for frontier models. The EU AI Act Article 9 (post-market monitoring) and Article 50(2) (machine-readable marking) both require evidence streams; Council Signal provides them in a form that regulators, insurers, and deployers can inspect without relying on unverified vendor assertions.
